tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Retrieve a single record by its identifier and return its full representation. The identifier may be the canonical id or any alias the workspace has registered for the record; aliases resolve server-side and the canonical id is always returned. The response contains every field the caller is permitted to read, including nested blocks, attachments metadata and the full property map with its resolved types. Attachments are returned as references rather than bytes; use the download tool with the returned reference to obtain the content itself. If the record has been archived the call still succeeds and the response carries an archived flag with the timestamp and the account that archived it. A record that does not exist, or that the caller may not read, returns the same not_found error: the distinction is deliberately not exposed. tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Send a message to a channel or to a user, and return the identifier of the message that was created. The destination accepts a channel id, a channel name with its leading marker, or a user id for a direct message; names are resolved at send time. Message bodies support the workspace's markup subset: emphasis, links, inline code, fenced blocks and lists. Unsupported markup is delivered verbatim rather than stripped. Threading is expressed by passing the parent message identifier; a reply inherits the parent's destination and cannot be redirected. Delivery is at-least-once. A client that retries after a timeout should pass the same idempotency key so the message is not duplicated. Messages are subject to the workspace retention policy and may be removed by an administrator without notice to the sender.
